s: ^He gave his life so that we might be free. Remember him that way.
^I will not weep for a slaver. Even one who turned at the eleventh hour.

c-0: ^I will. Have no doubt about that.
c-1: ^I can understand why you say that, but to me he seemed different. Alas, bleak as it may be, it doesn't matter now.

b: ^Gáspár, you idiot. A stubborn ox to the last.
^If he still had breath he would say he was being loyal, not stubborn.
^The guards are dead, and the breach is sealed. I have not felt like this in a long time... relieved. Hopeful. All thanks to your efforts.
^If Nándor had asked me only a few hours ago what our prospects of seeing the surface again were, I would have told him we would die down here. But thanks to you, we can finally leave this place.

4aa: ^Fat lot of good it did him in the end.

s: ^I for one won't miss him. *Spit.*
^Enough of this. You are our prisoners now.

c-0: ^Neither will I, I suppose. But it still seems like such a waste.

4ab: ^*Guard Réka looks like she wants to say something, but thinks better of it and nods instead.*

^If you do everything we say and do not resist, you will be treated much better than the guards have treated the branded. You have my word on that.
^Give me any excuse to harm you and I'll take it. Do not risk testing me.

4ac: ^*Réka looks to her weapon on the ground with regret, but then returns your gaze and nods.*

s: ^Good. Nándor, is there a place we can stow these two before we meet with Kastor? We don't want them being discovered before we make our move.
^Nándor, is there a place we can stow these two on our way to meet with Kastor? We don't want them being discovered before we make our move.

c-0: ^There's a room on the first floor the guards would keep slaves in when they didn't have time to supervise them. We can lock them in there and come back for them when we've won and found the key.

s: ^What if we don't succeed? Won't they be trapped in there?
^It will have to do. Let's get moving then.

c-0: ^I don't like to plan for that event, but if we fail then the guards should free them when they retake the mine. And we can leave them with some of the supplies from the stockroom on this level just in case.

4ada: ^Wait a moment. I just wanted to say that, with the breach sealed and the worms no longer a threat, I have not felt like this in a long time... relieved. Hopeful. All thanks to your efforts.

4b: ^The breach is sealed and the worms are no longer a threat. I have not felt like this in a long time... relieved. Hopeful. All thanks to your efforts.

s: ^Don't thank me yet. We still need to rally the other slaves and fight clear of the guards.
^Our cooperation was what made this possible. But let us not waste time, I am eager to return to camp.
^I have that effect on people. Now, if you're ready, I say we head for the surface.

weftHesitates_1a: ^*As the others move to leave, Weft hesitates.*

s: ^Weft? Is something the matter?

weftHesitates_1b: ^It's nothing. I'm just weary from battle.

s: ^You're normally better at lying than that. What is it?
^If you don't wish to discuss it, then we should keep moving.

weftHesitates_1c: ^I have no love for the guards, but after having slain some... I am forced to wonder if the same fate awaits me at the end of this revolution.
^The other branded hold no love for me. They may hate me even more than they hate the guards. When this road ends, what fate awaits one such as I?

s: ^They may hate you, but you haven't done anything to offend me yet. I can keep you safe from the others, if that remains so.
^That will be resolved at a later time. There is no use worrying about it now.
^You chose your fate when you turned against your fellow branded.

weftHesitates_1d: ^And what fate is that? Beheading? Hanging from the neck? Worse?

s: ^Nothing so dramatic. You'll be punished, but not with your ending. And after, you'll be free like the rest of us.
^A quick death, without humiliation. That will be preferable to the fates of many of the guards, believe me.
^I'm unable to say, but it won't be pleasant. Now keep up, we must be going.

c-1: ^*Weft hangs his head.* If that is the case, I will begin making my peace with it.
c-2: ^*Weft keeps his face a mask as he follows your lead.*

weftHesitates_1ea: ^When the stakes are so high, the only way I can trust what you say is if I am given collateral. And the most binding form of such is with an oath before the Gods.
weftHesitates_1eb: ^No! This cannot wait. No question could be more pressing; I need it answered!

s: ^If you showed such courage before the guards, you'd gain more respect. But if it will calm you, I don't plan to see you executed when this is over.
^You are not in a place to make demands. Now, we must move before the others begin to worry.

c-1: ^*Weft keeps his face a mask as he follows your lead.*

weftHesitates_1e: ^Swear it. Swear before the Gods that when this is all over I will leave this revolution with my life, lest They take my revenge for me after my passing.

s: ^I'm not going to do that. It isn't right to bother the Gods with a matter so trivial.
^Very well. I swear that your death will not come from punishment received from your fellow revolutionaries, or may the Gods conjure a punishment for me worthy of my failure.

c-0: ^That response does not fill me with hope. Let's just get moving before the others start to worry.
c-1: ^*Weft looks signifigantly relieved.* Thank you. Such an oath does much credit to your intentions.

^No, say your piece. I think they've more than earned the right to know.

^Carter and I are a part of a conspiracy to free the branded. Before being trapped on this floor, I had derived a plan in which we would eventually find weapons, gather the other branded, and fight the guards in open revolt.

s: ^I am aware of your part in the plan. Kastor asked me to find you and ask you which way the wind blows.
^Then perhaps you know which way the wind is blowing?
^This is very interesting. And I suppose this is the part where you ask me to help you?
^That sounds like the plan of a fool. The guards would break us like twigs.

c-0: ^You've divined my motive. What say you?

4e: ^Does it? Consider their casualties. Many guards died during the evacuation of this floor. There will never again come an opportunity like the present, for eventually they will replenish those numbers.

b: ^And we, just now, put to rest the myth of their invincibility. We should capitalize on their weakness now while we can, or else we will never again be able to!

4e: ^Nándor speaks true. His plan is sound, and the time is right. We should strike while the guards are weak and diminished.

s: ^If you have a plan, then I would hear it all before I commit myself to it.
^You are beginning to sway me. I will see where this goes.
^I won't be your lemming, no matter how appealing you try to make this cliff.

c-0: ^The first part of the plan was to learn where this camp lies on a map. The guards have kept the camp's location a secret since it was founded, but Carter has informed me we are currently within the Kingdom of Masons. If we can fight clear of the guards, we will not have to worry about more Lovashi taking back the camp for a long time.

^After that, we must gather weapons. Originally, I thought to find a way into the armory the guards keep in the barracks on the surface, but the mine itself has another cache of tools that we could plunder. The lockdown has made this part of the plan much easier.
